parts.label: (i)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Separate variables correctly and attempt integration of at least one side, e.g. $\int e^{-y}\,dy=\int xe^x\,dx$ [B1]. Obtain $-e^{-y}$ [B1; B0B1 is possible]. Start integration by parts and reach $xe^x\pm\int e^x\,dx$ [M1; B0B0M1A1 is possible]. Obtain $xe^x-e^x$, or equivalent [A1; B1B1M1A1 available without a constant]. Use $x=0,y=0$ to evaluate a constant, or use limits, in a solution containing nonzero $ae^{-y},bxe^x,ce^x$ terms [M1; this step must be seen]. Obtain a correct solution such as $e^{-y}=e^x-xe^x$ [A1]. Rearrange to $y=-\ln(1-x)-x$, or equivalent [A1; ISW]. Total 7.

parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Justify the statement, e.g. require $1-x>0$ for the logarithm to exist and hence $x<1$ [B1]. The reasoning must concern the range of $x$ and be relevant to their expression for $y$ involving $\ln(1-x)$. Total 1.
